reading.body:
The campus publishes 147.6 MW of combined utility power across 237,000 square feet of technical space. Utility power and IT load are not the same figure, and Centersquare does not publish a separate IT load number, so the usable compute capacity is not determinable from these facts alone. As a rough sense of scale, if one assumes 40 kW per rack as a common AI training density, 147.6 MW of total utility power would suggest a ceiling somewhere below 3,690 racks before accounting for power usage effectiveness overhead, mechanical losses, and lighting, meaning actual rack count at that density would be materially lower. At a more conservative 10 kW per rack, the same gross figure implies a ceiling near 14,760 racks, again before overhead. Neither number is Centersquare's claim.

The five certifications tell a narrow story. SOC 1 Type 2 and SOC 2 Type 2 qualify the campus for tenants whose auditors require attested controls over financial reporting systems and operational security respectively. PCI DSS qualifies it for workloads that touch payment card data. ISO 27001 qualifies it for tenants operating under information security management frameworks recognized across international supply chains. NIST 800-53 qualifies it for workloads aligned to US federal security and privacy controls. No tenants are published.

Illinois has 44 facilities mapped in this site's data, of which only 6 publish a MW figure, together totaling 236 MW. This campus at 147.6 MW would itself exceed that published state total, which means it ranks outside the top six by published MW in a state where most operators have not disclosed capacity figures, and the published state total as recorded here does not yet include this facility. That gap between 44 mapped facilities and 6 with published numbers is a reminder that the Illinois market is larger than the figures currently allow readers to measure.
